title: Gamma Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits and Limits
summary: Gamma pricing relies on monthly AI credit allowances that differ by plan. Review each tier's real limits to select the one matching your needs.
body_markdown:
## What Gamma Costs at Realistic Monthly Usage


**A freelancer needs roughly 150 credits a month** , a weekly founder about 200 and a three-person team about 600. These figures rest on an assumed 50 credits per deck, which is my estimate, not a Gamma number.


The table below turns each profile's deck count into credits needed. Compare the last column with the allowance on[gamma.app](https://gamma.app/) 's pricing page, and pick the cheapest plan above it.


Profile Decks per month Assumed credits per deck Credits needed


Freelancer 3 50 150


Founder, weekly decks 4 50 200


Three-person branded team 12 50 600


To put dollars on a profile, find the cheapest plan whose allowance covers its credits and read that plan's monthly price off the page. All three profiles fit inside Plus's 1,500 credits, so a higher price is buying export or branding terms, not volume.


Dollar totals stay unverified until the prices are, and for the team, multiply by the number of paid seats.


### Gamma Pricing for Freelancers Making Few Decks


Three decks at 50 credits is 150 credits, so a low-volume plan should suffice.


Image choice moves the number most. Gamma's[image model reference](https://developers.gamma.app/reference/image-model-accepted-values) lists four models at 2 credits and three at 8, so the same ten-image deck costs 20 or 80 credits in images alone. Default to a 2-credit model unless a client needs the premium look.


If you present weekly, that means four or five decks, so 200 to 250 credits. Gamma's image model reference lists one model at 5 credits and another at 6.


A founder who picks a mid-priced model for every slide pays two to three times the cheapest rate.


Twelve decks is 600 credits. Before credits, check export and branding rules, because a team that must remove Gamma branding may need a higher tier regardless of volume. That makes credits a floor, not the deciding factor.


To choose between two plans, divide the price gap by the cost of the extra credits you would otherwise run short of. If your peak month exceeds the allowance, move up.


If it only occasionally does, stay put and use cheaper image models. Over the 2-to-8-credit spread, that switch often saves more than the upgrade.
